account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: market rounds, lunch, town accounts, and tea with neighbour at the east-bank cottage. I am leaving tea for my office appointment. I have a feeling something may be happening without my knowing, but have not established any secret gathering or purpose.

The only distinctly curious remark was neighbour's statement that the baker says the bakery lights are 'simply everyday cheer.' I asked whether they were lit at an unusual hour, but have not received an answer explaining that. I have not personally observed unusual bakery lighting. It could simply be ordinary baking or decoration; I cannot yet say it signals an event.

Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat. I saw the baker stock bread at the market stall, and the baker said thirty-two fresh loaves were available. Those are consistent with normal business. The baker asked whether upcoming town gatherings would need bread, but reported no confirmed news. Neighbour likewise reported no definite dock changes and said they had attended no neighbourhood gatherings.

The secretary confirmed tea directly with neighbour and kept the appointment information in the office chest. During our accounts appointment, neither of us could identify the location of account records. The treasury contains 128 emeralds but no books. The secretary reported no new correspondence, reported outstanding council matters, or unusual funding requests, while acknowledging that the accounts themselves had not been examined. This is an unresolved administrative problem, not evidence of a concealed project. For now, the baker and neighbour are the people connected to the unexplained lighting remark; I do not know what, if anything, it is for.
